content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To care for an orchid indoors, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Check the moisture level of the potting medium (1 minute)
Step 2. Mix a balanced orchid fertilizer into a gallon of water (5 minutes)
Step 3. Wipe dust off the leaves with a damp cloth (10 minutes)
Step 4. Inspect the undersides of leaves for pests (3 minutes)
Step 5. Soak the orchid pot in the fertilizer solution (15 minutes)
Step 6. Prepare a humidity tray with pebbles and water (10 minutes)
Step 7. Sterilize pruning shears with rubbing alcohol (2 minutes)
Step 8. Apply a neem oil treatment to the foliage (5 minutes)
Step 9. Position the plant in a spot with bright, indirect light (2 minutes)
Step 10. Clean the exterior of the decorative cachepot (5 minutes)
Step 11. Measure the ambient room temperature (30 seconds)
Step 12. Research the specific species' dormancy requirements (20 minutes)
Step 13. Purchase a high-quality bark-based potting mix (1 hour)
Step 14. Trim away any dead or shriveled brown roots (10 minutes)
Step 15. Mist the aerial roots lightly (30 seconds)
Step 16. Stake the flower spike for support (5 minutes)
Step 17. Drain all excess water from the bottom of the pot (2 minutes)
Step 18. Set a calendar reminder for the next feeding (2 minutes)
Step 19. Check for signs of root rot through the clear liner (2 minutes)
Step 20. Gather all necessary repotting supplies (15 minutes)
Step 21. Place the pot on the humidity tray (1 minute)
Step 22. Adjust the blinds to prevent direct leaf scorch (1 minute)
Step 23. Wash the new orchid pot with soap (5 minutes)
Step 24. Label the pot with the date of the last treatment (2 minutes)
Step 25. Supplement with a bloom booster if needed (2 minutes)
Step 26. Log the maintenance activity in a garden journal (10 minutes)
Step 27. Gently loosen the old medium from the root ball (8 minutes)
Step 28. Fill a spray bottle with distilled water (2 minutes)
Step 29. Monitor the room's humidity percentage (24 hours)
Step 30. Repot the orchid into the fresh bark mix (20 minutes)
Step 31. Dilute the fertilizer to half-strength for safety (3 minutes)
Step 32. Soak the new bark mix in water to hydrate it (12 hours)
Step 33. Flush the potting medium with plain water to remove salts (10 minutes)
Step 34. Cut back the spent flower spike to the nearest node (5 minutes)
Step 35. Select a pot that is one size larger (15 minutes)
Step 36. Take a photograph of the orchid to track growth (1 minute)
Step 37. Check for new growth at the base of the plant (1 minute)
Step 38. Use a fan to improve air circulation around the plant (2 hours)
Step 39. Inspect the crown for any trapped water (2 minutes)
Step 40. Tap the pot to settle the new medium around roots (1 minute)
